title: 18 November 2026 — Original Practice Questions
qualityNote: 42 questions passed schema, source, exact/option-insensitive and semantic review. Eight candidates were rejected rather than weakening the zero-repeat standard.

questions.q: Under paragraph 2(1) of the Sixth Schedule, what is the maximum number of persons who may be nominated by the Governor to a District Council?
questions.e: Paragraph 2(1) caps a District Council at 30 members. Of these, not more than four may be nominated by the Governor; the remaining members are elected on the basis of adult suffrage.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule

questions.q: Under paragraph 2(6) of the Sixth Schedule, what is the normal term of an elected District Council member, unless the Council is sooner dissolved?
questions.e: The normal term is five years, counted from the date appointed for the Council's first meeting after the general election. The Schedule also permits earlier dissolution in specified circumstances.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule

questions.q: Two parties to a local dispute both belong to Scheduled Tribes and live within an autonomous district. Under paragraph 4(1), which body may be constituted to try such a case, subject to the Schedule's exceptions?
o: A village council or court constituted under the District Council
questions.e: Paragraph 4(1) allows the Regional Council or District Council to constitute village councils or courts for suits and cases where all parties belong to Scheduled Tribes within the relevant autonomous area. Cases covered by paragraph 5(1) are excluded.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule

questions.q: A case is first tried by a village council or court under paragraph 4(1). Which institution ordinarily exercises appellate power under paragraph 4(2)?
o: The relevant District or Regional Council, or a court constituted by it
questions.e: Paragraph 4(2) gives appellate power to the Regional Council or a court constituted by it; where there is no Regional Council for the area, the District Council or its constituted court exercises that role. The paragraph preserves the specified High Court and Supreme Court jurisdiction.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule

questions.q: Which activity is expressly included in a District Council's powers under paragraph 6(1) of the Sixth Schedule?
questions.e: Paragraph 6(1) specifically lists primary schools, dispensaries, markets, cattle pounds, ferries, fisheries, roads, road transport and waterways. It also permits the Council, with the Governor's prior approval, to regulate and control these facilities.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule

questions.q: Under paragraph 7(4) of the Sixth Schedule, which constitutional authority audits the accounts of District and Regional Councils?
questions.e: Paragraph 7(4) assigns the audit of District and Regional Council accounts to the Comptroller and Auditor-General. The audit reports are submitted to the Governor, who causes them to be laid before the Council.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule

questions.q: A District Council proposes to levy a tax on goods entering a market for sale there. Which provision expressly lists this taxing power?
questions.e: Paragraph 8(3)(c) expressly includes taxes on the entry of goods into a market for sale there, along with tolls on passengers and goods carried in ferries. This is distinct from the Council's law-making subjects under paragraph 3.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule

questions.q: The State Government and a District Council disagree over the share of royalties from a mineral lease in an autonomous district. Who determines the disputed amount under paragraph 9(2)?
questions.e: Under paragraph 9(2), a dispute over the royalty share is referred to the Governor. The amount determined by the Governor is treated as payable to the District Council, and the decision is final under that paragraph.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule

questions.q: What minimum majority of the total membership of a District Council is required to pass regulations under paragraph 10 of the Sixth Schedule?
questions.e: The proviso to paragraph 10(2) requires a majority of not less than three-fourths of the total membership. The paragraph concerns regulations controlling money-lending and trading by persons other than Scheduled Tribes resident in the district.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule

questions.q: Under paragraph 11 of the Sixth Schedule, when do laws, rules and regulations made by a District or Regional Council acquire the force of law?
o: On publication in the Official Gazette of the State
After approval by the Lok Sabha
Thirty days after being sent to the Governor
questions.e: Paragraph 11 requires these laws, rules and regulations to be published forthwith in the State's Official Gazette. They acquire the force of law on that publication.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Constitution of India (2024 edition), Sixth Schedule

questions.q: Which Meghalaya department coordinates the work of the Autonomous District Councils with other State Government departments and the Government of India?
o: Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms
questions.e: The Meghalaya Government portal states that the District Council Affairs Department coordinates the work between the District Councils, other State Government departments and the Government of India. This is an administrative coordination function, not direct implementation of every Council scheme.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Government of Meghalaya—District Council Affairs Department.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Government of Meghalaya—District Council Affairs Department

questions.q: An Autonomous District Council submits a Bill or regulation to the State. If the Department finds it legally in order under the Sixth Schedule and the applicable Council rules, what does the Meghalaya District Council Affairs Department do next?
o: Recommends it to the Governor for assent or approval
Sends it directly to the Supreme Court
Publishes it as a Central Act
Places it before the Union Public Service Commission
questions.e: The Department examines Council Bills, regulations and rules for legality under the Sixth Schedule and the Assam and Meghalaya Autonomous Districts (Constitution of District Councils) Rules, 1951, as amended. If the proposal is in order, it is recommended to the Governor for assent or approval.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Government of Meghalaya—District Council Affairs Department.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Government of Meghalaya—District Council Affairs Department

questions.q: Which rare citrus species is protected by the gene sanctuary located in the buffer zone of the Nokrek Biosphere Reserve?
questions.e: The Meghalaya Biodiversity Board identifies Citrus indica, locally known as Memang Narang, as the rare citrus conserved in the gene sanctuary in Nokrek's buffer zone. The question tests the species-level conservation fact rather than the general location of Nokrek.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Meghalaya Biodiversity Board—Protected Areas.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Meghalaya Biodiversity Board—Protected Areas

questions.q: According to the Meghalaya Biodiversity Board, what is the elevation of Nokrek Peak, the highest point in the Tura Mountain Range?
questions.e: The Meghalaya Biodiversity Board gives Nokrek Peak's elevation as 1,418 metres above sea level. The page also identifies Nokrek Ridge National Park as the core of the Nokrek Biosphere Reserve.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Meghalaya Biodiversity Board—Protected Areas.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Meghalaya Biodiversity Board—Protected Areas

questions.q: How many Important Bird Area (IBA) sites does the Meghalaya Biodiversity Board identify in the State?
questions.e: The Board's Important Bird Areas page states that nine IBA sites have been identified in Meghalaya. The list includes sites in the Khasi, Jaintia and Garo Hills regions.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Meghalaya Biodiversity Board—Important Bird Areas.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Meghalaya Biodiversity Board—Important Bird Areas

questions.q: The Meghalaya Biodiversity Board describes the Tawny-breasted Wren Babbler as restricted to which broad geographical range?
o: Khasi Hills of Meghalaya and Manipur
questions.e: The Board reports the species from the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya and Manipur, generally at elevations of about 1,000–2,000 metres. It inhabits the understorey of broadleaved evergreen forests, forest edges and nearby scrub.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Meghalaya Biodiversity Board—Important Bird Areas.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Meghalaya Biodiversity Board—Important Bird Areas

questions.q: Which Meghalaya site is specifically listed by the State Biodiversity Board as an Important Bird Area and is also a well-known sacred grove?
questions.e: Mawphlang Sacred Grove appears in the Meghalaya Biodiversity Board's list of nine Important Bird Areas. The other options are well-known places, but they are not the site identified in that IBA list.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Meghalaya Biodiversity Board—Important Bird Areas.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Meghalaya Biodiversity Board—Important Bird Areas

questions.q: The CERT-In Cyber Security Directions dated 28 April 2022 were issued under which provision of the Information Technology Act, 2000?
questions.e: CERT-In's official Directions page identifies the directions as issued under Section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000. The 2022 directions specifically invoke the power under sub-section (6).
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B

questions.q: Which group correctly lists the entities expressly named in the 28 April 2022 CERT-In Directions for mandatory reporting of specified cyber incidents?
o: Service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates and government organisations
Only internet service providers and telecom operators
questions.e: Direction (ii) names service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates and government organisations. The reporting requirement is not confined to banks or to government ministries alone.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B

questions.q: A covered organisation becomes aware of a cyber incident listed in Annexure I at 10:15 a.m. By what time must it report the incident to CERT-In under the 2022 Directions?
questions.e: The Directions require the specified incidents to be reported within six hours of noticing the incident or being brought to notice of it. Six hours after 10:15 a.m. is 4:15 p.m.; the clock does not wait for a completed forensic investigation.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B

questions.q: An organisation cannot obtain every detail requested in CERT-In's incident-reporting form before the six-hour deadline. What does the official CERT-In FAQ advise?
o: Wait until every field is confirmed before reporting
Report only after the incident is fully closed
Provide the information available at the time and send additional details later within a reasonable time
Report only to the cloud vendor
questions.e: CERT-In's FAQ says the entity may provide the information available at the time of reporting and submit additional information later within a reasonable time. Missing details do not justify delaying the initial report beyond the prescribed period.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CERT-In—FAQ on Cyber Security Directions.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CERT-In—FAQ on Cyber Security Directions

questions.q: For how long must covered entities securely maintain logs of all their ICT systems under the 2022 CERT-In Directions?
questions.e: Direction (iv) requires logs of all ICT systems to be enabled and securely maintained for a rolling period of 180 days, within Indian jurisdiction. This is a log-retention requirement, not the six-hour incident-reporting deadline.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B

questions.q: Which systems are covered by the log-enablement requirement in Direction (iv) of CERT-In's 2022 Directions?
o: All ICT systems of the covered entity
Only systems that have already suffered an incident
questions.e: The direction refers to logs of all ICT systems, not merely internet-facing servers or systems already known to be compromised. The logs must also be securely retained for the prescribed rolling period.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B

questions.q: Which time sources are specified by CERT-In for synchronising ICT system clocks under the 2022 Directions?
o: NIC or NPL time servers, or servers traceable to them
A server chosen independently by each employee
The device manufacturer's factory clock only
questions.e: The Directions require covered entities to synchronise their ICT system clocks with the Network Time Protocol servers of NIC or NPL, or with servers traceable to those time sources. Consistent timestamps help correlate events during incident response.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B

questions.q: What organisational arrangement must a covered entity make under the CERT-In Directions so that CERT-In can communicate about cyber incidents and compliance?
o: Register every employee as a CERT-In officer
Create a new statutory audit committee
questions.e: The Directions require each covered entity to designate a Point of Contact. CERT-In communications seeking information or issuing directions are routed to that designated contact, whose details are furnished in the prescribed format.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B

questions.q: A government organisation's data is stored on a third-party cloud platform, and a cyber incident affects that data. Does use of the third-party platform by itself remove the organisation's CERT-In reporting obligation?
o: Yes, the cloud provider alone must report
Yes, if the data centre is outside the State
No; the FAQ says the Directions apply to entities for reporting even where their data is affected in a third party's system
Only if the organisation owns the physical server
questions.e: CERT-In's FAQ addresses incidents affecting data stored in a third party's systems and states that the Directions apply to all entities insofar as reporting of a cyber incident is concerned. Outsourcing storage does not by itself remove the entity's reporting duty.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CERT-In—FAQ on Cyber Security Directions.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CERT-In—FAQ on Cyber Security Directions

questions.q: Which of the following is expressly included among the cyber incidents listed in Annexure I of CERT-In's 2022 Directions?
o: A routine software update completed successfully
A data breach or data leak
A staff member changing a desktop wallpaper
questions.e: Annexure I includes data breaches and data leaks among the cyber incidents that must be reported by covered entities within the prescribed time. Routine maintenance without a cyber incident is not, by itself, the incident described in this option.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CERT-In—Directions under Section 70B

questions.q: When tax deducted under Section 51 is reflected in the deductor's return, in which electronic ledger does the deductee claim the credit under Section 51(5)?
questions.e: Section 51(5) provides that the deductee claims the amount deducted as tax in the electronic cash ledger when it is reflected in the deductor's return. GST TDS credit should not be confused with input tax credit in the electronic credit ledger.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. CBIC—CGST Act, 2017, Section 51.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: CBIC—CGST Act, 2017, Section 51

questions.q: A regular vehicle (not carrying over-dimensional cargo) is expected to travel 310 km. Under the ordinary-cargo distance rule, how many days of e-way bill validity are allowed?
questions.e: For ordinary cargo, one day of validity is allowed for every 200 km or part of the distance. A 310 km journey includes the first 200 km plus part of the next 200 km, so two days are allowed.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. National E-Way Bill System—Official FAQ on validity.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: National E-Way Bill System—Official FAQ on validity

questions.q: From 1 January 2025, the National E-Way Bill System's API validation generally prevents generation of an e-way bill when the underlying document date is more than how many days before the generation date?
questions.e: The official E-Way Bill System validation note states that, from 1 January 2025, an e-way bill cannot be generated through the API for a document date more than 180 days before the generation date. This is a portal validation, distinct from the distance-based validity period.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. National E-Way Bill System—Additional Validations (18 December 2024).
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: National E-Way Bill System—Additional Validations (18 December 2024)

questions.q: Under the National E-Way Bill System validation effective from 1 January 2025, an e-way bill cannot be extended beyond how many days from its original generation date?
questions.e: The official validation note sets a 360-day cap measured from the e-way bill's generation date. Even where an extension is otherwise permitted, the resulting validity cannot go beyond that maximum horizon.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. National E-Way Bill System—Additional Validations (18 December 2024).
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: National E-Way Bill System—Additional Validations (18 December 2024)

questions.q: According to the National E-Way Bill System's official updates, from which date did two-factor authentication become mandatory for all taxpayers and transporters using the system?
questions.e: The official E-Way Bill System updates record that two-factor authentication became mandatory for all taxpayers and transporters from 1 April 2025. This is an operational portal-security requirement, not a change to the GST tax rate.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. National E-Way Bill System—Latest Updates.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: National E-Way Bill System—Latest Updates

questions.q: As recorded in the National E-Way Bill System release notes dated 30 July 2026, what was the status of the proposed EWB Closure functionality and mandatory Ship-to GSTIN changes?
o: Both were permanently cancelled by Parliament
They applied only to composition taxpayers
questions.e: The official release notes updated on 30 July 2026 state that the recent changes concerning EWB Closure and mandatory Ship-to GSTIN were kept on hold. This is a dated operational-status question; verify the release notes again before using it after the verification date.

questions.q: Which geological unit is identified by the Geological Survey of India as part of the principal basement geology of Meghalaya beneath the Shillong Group?
questions.e: The Geological Survey of India's North Eastern Region briefing book describes Meghalaya as comprising mainly the Precambrian Gneissic Complex and the Shillong Group of sedimentary rocks. The Gneissic Complex is the older basement unit in the relationship described.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section

questions.q: Which rock sequence does the Geological Survey of India identify as characteristic of the Shillong Group in Meghalaya?
questions.e: The GSI briefing book describes the Shillong Group as a conglomerate-quartzite-phyllite sequence. It is a sedimentary/metasedimentary sequence, not the basaltic or granitic alternatives listed.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section

questions.topic: Meghalaya geology—Tertiary sediments and Sylhet Traps
questions.q: Along which margins of the Meghalaya Plateau does GSI describe a near-complete sequence of Tertiary sediments overlying the volcanic suite of the Sylhet Traps?
questions.e: The GSI briefing book places the near-complete Tertiary sediment sequence along the eastern and southern rims of the plateau, overlying the volcanic suite of the Sylhet Traps. The question tests the spatial relationship rather than simply naming a rock type.
tags: Meghalaya geology—Tertiary sediments and Sylhet Traps
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section

questions.q: Which natural hazard does the Geological Survey of India specifically identify as affecting the southern flank of the Meghalaya Plateau?
questions.e: The GSI briefing book states that the southern flank of the plateau is prone to landslides. This is a regional geological-hazard observation; it does not mean that every slope or site has the same level of risk.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section

questions.q: The Geological Survey of India describes Meghalaya's major limestone resources as occurring particularly in Tertiary rocks across which hill regions?
questions.e: The GSI briefing book identifies substantial limestone resources in Tertiary rocks of the Jaintia, Khasi and Garo Hills. It lists deposits at several localities across all three regions.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section

questions.q: According to the GSI briefing book, the largest limestone deposit in Meghalaya occurs in which geological unit and locality?
o: Shella Formation of the Jaintia Group around the Litang River Valley
Tura Sandstone around the Simsang River
questions.e: GSI identifies the largest limestone deposit in Meghalaya in the Shella Formation rocks of the Jaintia Group, of Eocene age, around the Litang River Valley in Jaintia Hills. The answer combines the formation, group and locality to avoid confusion with other mineral occurrences.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section

questions.q: The Meghalaya Government portal explains that the stalagmite in Mawjymbuin Cave formed through deposition from mineralised solutions. Which compound is deposited to build this feature?
questions.e: The State portal attributes the Mawjymbuin Cave stalagmite to deposition of calcium carbonate from dripping mineralised solutions. Calcium carbonate accumulates over time to build the cave formation; it is not salt or iron sulphide.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Government of Meghalaya—Shillong district profile, Mawjymbuin Cave.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Government of Meghalaya—Shillong district profile, Mawjymbuin Cave

questions.q: Which rock is specifically named by GSI as one of the Khasi Basic-Ultrabasic Intrusives occurring in Meghalaya?
questions.e: The GSI briefing book lists epidiorite, metagabbro and metadolerite among the basic intrusives in Meghalaya. Metagabbro is the only listed intrusive rock among these options.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section

questions.q: The Gondwana coalfields of Meghalaya are exposed in which basin in the north-western corner of the Garo Hills?
questions.e: GSI states that Meghalaya's Gondwana coalfields are restricted to the Garo Hills and exposed in the Singrimari Basin near the north-western corner of the hills, bordering Dhubri district of Assam. The report distinguishes these from the Tertiary coalfields elsewhere in the Garo Hills.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Geological Survey of India—North Eastern Region Briefing Book, Meghalaya section.
